problem_statement: A node configured to allow more than one IPv6 address to be associated with a single link-layer neighbor can only retain one such address. When a neighbor is reachable over a link that owns both a link-local address (fe80::202:2:2:2) and a unique-local address (fd00::202:2:2:2), the node successfully answers a ping to one of them but fails to answer the ping to the other, and the neighbor-cache inspection reports only a single IPv6 address bound to the neighbor's link-layer address (0002.0002.0002.0002) instead of both. The required behavior is that, when the multi-address capability is enabled, both the link-local and the unique-local address of the same neighbor are cached against the same link-layer address, both remain reachable (state Reachable), and a neighbor-cache query lists the two IPv6 addresses side by side for that single link-layer neighbor.
causal_chain: The two failing scenarios build the mote with the multi-IPv6-address neighbor capability enabled and drive it through a script that pings the neighbor's link-local address, then its unique-local address, then issues the neighbor-cache query, asserting that both IPv6 addresses appear for the one link-layer address in the Reachable state. Before the production change the neighbor cache keys entries strictly by link-layer address and holds at most one IPv6 address per link-layer neighbor, so the second address cannot be represented/resolved and the assertion that two IPv6 addresses are associated with the same link-layer address cannot be satisfied; the single-address ping scenarios (the pass-to-pass set) exercise only one address per neighbor and are unaffected.
